question: What term describes a steady, predictable presence of a disease within a specific geographic zone?
explanation: An endemic disease remains constantly present at a baseline level within a particular region. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h1)

question: When does a local health event officially qualify as an outbreak?

options.A: When disease cases suddenly exceed the normal expected baseline in a community
options.B: When international travel restrictions are enforced by the ministry of health
options.C: When a single patient arrives at the primary health clinic with a rare infection
options.D: When health authorities declare a nationwide emergency due to rising malaria

explanation: An outbreak is defined by a sudden, unexpected spike in cases above normal local patterns. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h1)

question: Cholera outbreaks in rural communities are most frequently linked to which transmission pathway?
explanation: Cholera bacteria spread primarily through drinking water contaminated with sewage or fecal matter. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h2)

question: A patient presents with high fever, body aches, and a history of mosquito bites in a swampy area. What type of transmission has occurred?
explanation: Insects such as mosquitoes act as living vectors that carry and transmit infectious pathogens to humans. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a case definition during a disease outbreak?

options.A: To assign blame to the community members who caused the contamination
options.B: To accurately identify and count suspected or confirmed cases in the population
options.C: To determine the financial cost of purchasing treatment drugs for the hospital
options.D: To provide immediate surgical intervention for severe complications

explanation: A case definition gives healthcare workers uniform criteria to decide who has the disease and needs reporting. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h3)

question: Why is daily clinic recordkeeping vital for community health nurses monitoring an outbreak?

options.A: it prevents the federal government from auditing local clinic funds.
options.B: It guarantees that every patient will receive free medications.
options.C: It helps spot unusual clusters of symptoms or patient origins early.
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory confirmation of blood samples.

explanation: Reviewing clinic logs allows nurses to notice when disease incidence rises above normal seasonal expectations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h3)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Verify the clinical diagnosis and laboratory results
options.B: Close down all local markets and schools
options.C: Conduct a mass vaccination campaign across the state
options.D: Hold a press conference on national television

explanation: Before declaring an outbreak, the nurse must ensure the reported illnesses are accurately diagnosed. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h4)

question: Why do epidemiologists construct an epidemic curve during an active outbreak investigation?

options.A: To determine which healthcare workers deserve hazard allowances
options.B: To visualize the time course of the outbreak and identify the likely exposure period
options.C: To prove that the local government failed to provide clean drinking water
options.D: To calculate the exact monetary damages caused by the disease in the market

explanation: An epidemic curve plots cases by time of onset, helping reveal whether exposure was point-source or continuous. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h4)

question: What is the difference between isolation and quarantine in public health practice?

options.A: Isolation takes place at home, while quarantine occurs inside an intensive care unit.
options.B: Isolation is voluntary, whereas quarantine requires a court order from a judge.
options.C: Isolation applies only to animals, while quarantine applies exclusively to human patients.
options.D: Isolation separates sick people with a disease, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people.

explanation: Isolation deals with confirmed infectious patients, while quarantine holds those who had contact and might develop illness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h5)

question: Which intervention directly targets the environmental transmission route during a waterborne cholera outbreak?

options.A: Administering therapeutic antibiotics to all pregnant women
options.B: Conducting door-to-door educational seminars on personal hygiene
options.C: Chlorination and boiling of community drinking water sources
options.D: Placing all infected patients in locked isolation wards

explanation: Treating water supplies directly cuts off the vehicle spreading the cholera pathogen to the community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h5)

question: Why is involving local community and religious leaders essential during an outbreak response?

options.A: They possess formal medical degrees required to prescribe isolation medications.
options.B: They are responsible for funding the procurement of vaccines from abroad.
options.C: They help build trust and encourage compliance with health directives among residents.
options.D: They act as laboratory technicians to test contaminated water samples.

explanation: Community leaders hold influence and can dispel harmful rumors, ensuring people follow vital health safety advice. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h6)

question: Which practice should community health nurses actively promote to prevent the spread of fecal-oral diseases?

options.A: Consuming unpasteurized milk from local cattle
options.B: Avoiding all contact with healthcare clinics
options.C: Frequent handwashing with soap and clean water
options.D: Sleeping outdoors without treated mosquito nets

explanation: Proper hand hygiene removes pathogens from the hands, stopping the fecal-oral transmission cycle. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h6)
